draft.title: Patterns in the groups
card: The Group 1 metals, such as lithium, sodium and potassium, react strongly with water. They make hydrogen gas and an alkaline solution.
The reaction gets stronger down the group. Potassium reacts more strongly than sodium, and sodium more than lithium.
The noble gases, such as helium, neon and argon, hardly react at all.
Their outer shells are full, which makes their atoms very stable. They have little reason to react with other elements.
draft.remember: Group 1 reacts strongly, more so down the group. Group 18 hardly reacts because its outer shells are full.

a.q: Why do the noble gases hardly react with other elements?
opts: They have no electrons at all
They are too light to react
a.why: A full outer shell makes an atom stable, so it has little reason to react. Empty shells are wrong because noble gas atoms do have electrons.
a.clue: Think about what is true of the outer shell.

b.q: A teacher drops lithium, sodium and potassium into separate bowls of water. Which reacts most strongly?
b.why: Reactions get stronger down Group 1, and potassium is lowest of the three. Sodium is tempting because it is the middle, but it reacts less strongly than potassium.
b.clue: Which metal sits lowest in the group?

problems.detail: Why (a) dismisses 'Their outer shells are empty' by saying noble gas atoms do have electrons. That reasoning answers the 'no electrons at all' option instead, so it does not explain why the 'empty' option is wrong and may confuse students.
